(1) we introduce a novel model of neural activity in the C. elegans connectome, (2) we demonstrate that connectomic constraints improve the predictive performance of our model, and (3) we demonstrate that realistic conductance-based models are more accurate than current-based models for the C. elegan s nervous system.

we developed a model of the C. elegans connectome that can predict the activity of withheld neurons significantly better than models without connectomic constraints, and that conductance-based models provide significantly better predictions than models with current-based synapses.

the development of a mechanistic, data-driven whole-brain model of C. elegans neural activity.

the CC-LVM is a promising approach for learning mechanistic whole-brain models from calcium imaging data.
our CC-LVM can learn the activity of neurons that were not observed, and that this is improved when using conductance-based synapse models.

our model provides an interpretable, biophysically plausible model of the worm nervous system that is constrained by the connectome, and that the model can be used to predict the activity in unobserved neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CC-LVM is able to provide a mechanistic model of the whole-brain neural activity, and the connectomic constraints are crucial for this purpose.

we developed a framework that allows us to learn the dynamics of an entire neural system, and applied it to a large scale experimental dataset, where the connectome was used to provide a prior on the model parameters.

the CC-LVM is a powerful tool that can learn a generative model for the neural activity of the entire C elegans nervous system, constrained by the connectome and the biophysical properties of the neurons, and can be applied to a broad range of neural systems with similar data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the connectome is a powerful prior constraint for inferring latent neural dynamics from calcium imaging data.
a mechanistic generative model of neural activity can be learned from data, and that connectomic constraints can improve the accuracy of the model.
connectomic constraints can be used to improve the predictive power of mechanistic models of neural activity, and that biophysical detail is crucial for such models to be useful in practice.
